Carmen L: FYI - kv-cache instance kv-canary-9 OOMed twice during the afternoon ramp. Logs show `fatal error: runtime: out of memory`. Uploading pprofs to s3://redwood/debug/kv/5012345678/
Vikram S: can you drop a short pprof topline? want to know if this is retained-live or fragmentation.
Carmen L: pprof top (alloc_space):
```
pprof: top
62MB   runtime.mallocgc
35MB   github.com/redwood/runtime/kv.(*Shard).applyBatch
14MB   github.com/redwood/runtime/cache.newEntry
```
Noah P: applyBatch dominating again. This smells like post-bulk-import churn we've seen before. Immediate mitigation: flip a soft-heap-cap to 70% for the canary slice + ephemeral eviction TTL=45s. Heather, can you own the soft-cap flip and validate?
Heather J: Yup. I'll apply the cap and watch evict logs/latency. ETA 30m.
trace-bot: Created INF-5401: "kv-canary-9 OOM triage + profiling" and INF-5402: "apply soft-heap-cap + ephemeral eviction kv-canary-9" (assigned: Heather J) :white_check_mark:
Vikram S: I'll take profiling. Plan: heap snapshots at t0, t+5m, t+20m; run `go tool pprof -inuse_space -alloc_space` and run a symbol diff. Also capture allocation stacks for large slices. I'll post a diff script to INF-5401. ETA: tomorrow morning.
Carmen L: Also proposing a GC sensitivity experiment: baseline -> GOGC=80 -> GOGC=200 on a small cohort and measure fragmentation ratio, CPU, and p99 latency. Owner: Noah?
Noah P: I can run GC runs. Will capture CPU/latency/evict_rate tradeoffs. If earlier GC reduces frag ratio but CPU cost is acceptable, we can consider automated temporary GOGC for canaries. Due: 2026-04-06.
Vikram S: Long-term signal ask: add `slab_contiguous_free` and `slab_total_alloc` per-shard plus `live_object_count` to Prom. That will help quickly determine fragmentation vs live growth. Owner suggestion: Vikram for schema, Carmen for Console wiring.
Heather J: Soft-cap applied at 15:20; early numbers: evict_count=102 in 25m, median latency +3ms, p99 steady. No new OOMs in watch window so far. Posting logs to INF-5402.
Carmen L: Action recap (adding to postmortem follow-ups doc):
- A1: Heap snapshots & symbol-diff script (owner: Vikram S) — capture across next two canary runs — due: 2026-04-02
- A2: Temporary soft-heap-cap + ephemeral eviction validation (owner: Heather J) — monitor and post logs — due: 2026-03-29
- A3: GC sensitivity experiment (owner: Noah P) — run GOGC variants and collect CPU/latency/frag metrics — due: 2026-04-06
- A4: Frag metrics exporter (owners: Vikram S / Carmen L) — `slab_contiguous_free`, `slab_total_alloc`, `live_object_count` prototype + dashboard mock — due: 2026-04-13
- A5: Bulk-import regression harness + compaction test (owner: storage-team) — reproduce applyBatch spike and validate compaction behavior — due: 2026-04-20
- A6: Follow-up retro & recurring-pattern decision (owner: Carmen L) — sync and decide RFC trigger if 3x recurrence in 30 days — due: 2026-04-15
Noah P: If heap diffs show many small retained slices and low contiguous_free, we should consider a slab-coalescing PoC or allocator-path RFC. Marking as contingent R&D.
Vikram S: I'll upload the initial diff script and point at INF-5401. Please put any ad-hoc notes in the ticket rather than DMs.
Heather J: Will validate eviction traces and attach a short validation snippet to INF-5402 after 30m.
Carmen L: Thanks — closing loop here once Vikram posts diffs and Noah posts GC experiment results. We'll consolidate timelines in the postmortem follow-up doc and mark recurring-pattern if reproduced. :thumbsup:
